minutes.headline: Board voted to study creating an assistant director role while pushing ahead to fill Pauline's departing post
minutes.summary: The Council on Aging debated whether to advertise a straightforward outreach coordinator replacement for the departing Pauline or instead pursue a new assistant director position that would absorb outreach duties; members voted to have the Town Manager research the assistant director option's cost and duties while also voting to urge the administration to move ahead hiring Pauline's replacement without delay. The board also voted to have its Chair represent the COA before the Select Board on Article 12 (town warrant notification), heard financial and director's reports, recognized a departing staff member, and tabled bylaws and lobby-furnishings items to a later meeting.

what_happened.line: Board voted to have the Town Manager research creating a new assistant director position, its cost and duties.
Board separately voted to urge hiring a replacement for the departing outreach coordinator without delay.
Board voted to have its Chair represent the Council on Aging before the Select Board on Article 12, town warrant notification.
Bylaws feedback and a lobby-furnishings purchase were tabled to a later meeting.

why_it_matters: A new assistant director position would add a funded town staff role, a decision that can affect future budget requests and, members noted, could bear on a future property tax override.
Voting to fill the departing coordinator's post separately from the study means senior outreach services continue while the larger staffing question is researched.
Article 12 concerns how the town posts and notifies residents of town meeting warrants, and now goes to the Select Board with the COA Chair representing the board's position.
